issue.title: Emoji in generic Markdown ref PDFs print as missing glyphs (DejaVu-only fonts, no emoji fallback)
issue.description:
Generic Markdown `bob ref create` renders (pandoc → XeLaTeX, `render_temp_pdf_from` in `src/native/highlights_ref/create.rs`) set `mainfont=DejaVu Serif`, `sansfont=DejaVu Sans`, `monofont=DejaVu Sans Mono` with no fallback face. Emoji used in agent research reports (🍅, ✅, ⚠️, …) therefore print as missing glyphs, and the PDF text layer carries U+0000 for them. Note snapshots do not have this problem: `note_snapshot/note.tex` ships `NotoEmoji-Regular.ttf` as `\BobFallbackFont` and routes uncovered codepoints through the glyph table in `note.lua`.

Evidence: `~/bob/lib/chat/now_tag_vs_in_progress_status.pdf`, page 2. The PyMuPDF text is `gives it a \x00. The hooks…` where the source Markdown has `gives it a 🍅`. The embedded fonts are DejaVu only. The same tofu appears in fresh renders with bob's pandoc flags (see `compare_current.png` in the research assets of `research:202610/ref_create_tables_vs_pdfkit_cell_selection__cld.md`).

Likely fix: reuse the note-snapshot font/glyph-table fallback (or a fontspec fallback) for the generic Markdown route, so uncovered codepoints render with Noto Emoji and extract as the right characters.

task_type_fields.impact: Every chat/research reference PDF that uses emoji shows tofu boxes, and highlighted quotes that cover them lose the character
task_type_fields.location: src/native/highlights_ref/create.rs render_temp_pdf_from (-V mainfont/sansfont/monofont DejaVu, no fallback)
task_type_fields.repro: bob ref create on any Markdown file containing an emoji such as 🍅, then extract the PDF text (e.g. ~/bob/lib/chat/now_tag_vs_in_progress_status.pdf page 2 shows 'gives it a \x00.'); the glyph prints as tofu

issue.creation_reason: Found while researching table rendering for Highlights: emoji in chat-report PDFs render as tofu and extract as NUL, which hurts readability and corrupts Highlights quote text.
